top_choice_rationale: P001 rewards a genuinely new principle, the magic-wavelength lattice that cancels the light shift and lets many atoms be interrogated without perturbation, with a narrow citation and a clean originator (Katori) and perfecter (Ye) allocation. The result has been reproduced and compared at the 10^-18 level in several independent laboratories, and it exposed new physics (blackbody and hyperpolarisability shifts, many-body spin exchange, gravitational redshift within one cloud). P002 is a deep result, but its credit allocation (Kane, Molenkamp, Xue, without Mele, Hasan or Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang) and the merger of two separate experiments, plus overlap with the 2016 prize, leave it less settled. No award is the weakest option given a mature, well-attributed candidate.
recusal_note: No link to Katori or Ye as collaborators, but I am a theorist in precision atomic structure close to the optical-clock field and a long-time collaborator of 2023 laureate Anne L'Huillier; none of this appears to require recusal from the credited work.
